{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.45,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "polarity",
      "components": ["Q1", "U6"],
      "pins": ["Q1.2", "Q1.3", "U6.1", "U6.6"],
      "nets": ["+5V", "USBC_VBUS_IN"],
      "observed": "Q1 (Q_PMOS_GSD) has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. U6 (LTC4412) has VIN (pin 1) on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (pin 6) on +5V, so the controller treats +5V as the load side and VBUS as the input.",
      "expected": "For an LTC4412 ideal-diode OR-ing stage the PFET source should sit on the input (VIN/USBC_VBUS_IN) and the drain on the load (+5V). That blocks reverse current from +5V back onto the USB input, which the note in the spec says is the main purpose of this stage.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U6\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"VIN\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U6\") (pin \"6\") (pinfunction \"SENSE\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "USB input \"OR-ing\"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, `U6`)"}
      ],
      "impact": "The PFET body diode conducts from +5V back to the USB VBUS pin, so the reverse-current protection the stage is meant to provide does not work. Backfeed from the 5 V rail onto the USB input can occur.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "short_to_ground",
      "components": ["D30", "R60"],
      "pins": ["D30.2", "D30.4", "R60.1", "R60.2"],
      "nets": ["ESTOP_OUT", "Net-(D30-K2)"],
      "observed": "The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode (A2, pin 4) directly on ESTOP_OUT and its cathode (K2, pin 2) through R60 also on ESTOP_OUT. The LED is therefore connected across a single net and carries no current.",
      "expected": "Each LED half should have its anode and cathode on different nets, with the series resistor between the cathode and a defined sink or the other end of the circuit.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R60 Net-_D30-K2_ ESTOP_OUT 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The LED indicator tied to the E-stop output never lights, and R60 is a loop with no useful function. The indicator fails silently.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D4", "D14", "D23"],
      "pins": ["D4.2", "D14.2", "D23.2"],
      "nets": ["/LED_3.3V_POWER_SW"],
      "observed": "The anodes of D4, D14 and D23 are all on net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW, and no other pin or source is connected to that net.",
      "expected": "The anodes of these status LEDs need a supply (+3V3 or a switched 3.3 V rail). Their cathodes are driven by the CM4 Ethernet and activity LED lines, so a floating anode means the LEDs cannot light.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"32\") (name \"/LED_3.3V_POWER_SW\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D4\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The Ethernet and power/activity indicator LEDs (D4, D14, D23) stay dark because their anode net has no source.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The most likely deviation is that Q1 is wired with source on +5V and drain on the USB VBUS input, the reverse of what the LTC4412 VIN/SENSE usage requires, which would defeat the reverse-current protection. Two weaker candidates are a dual-LED half shorted onto ESTOP_OUT and status LED anodes with no supply."
}

anomalies.observed: Q1 (Q_PMOS_GSD) has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. U6 (LTC4412) has VIN (pin 1) on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (pin 6) on +5V, so the controller treats +5V as the load side and VBUS as the input.
anomalies.expected: For an LTC4412 ideal-diode OR-ing stage the PFET source should sit on the input (VIN/USBC_VBUS_IN) and the drain on the load (+5V). That blocks reverse current from +5V back onto the USB input, which the note in the spec says is the main purpose of this stage.
anomalies.impact: The PFET body diode conducts from +5V back to the USB VBUS pin, so the reverse-current protection the stage is meant to provide does not work. Backfeed from the 5 V rail onto the USB input can occur.

anomalies.observed: The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode (A2, pin 4) directly on ESTOP_OUT and its cathode (K2, pin 2) through R60 also on ESTOP_OUT. The LED is therefore connected across a single net and carries no current.
anomalies.expected: Each LED half should have its anode and cathode on different nets, with the series resistor between the cathode and a defined sink or the other end of the circuit.
anomalies.impact: The LED indicator tied to the E-stop output never lights, and R60 is a loop with no useful function. The indicator fails silently.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of D4, D14 and D23 are all on net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW, and no other pin or source is connected to that net.
anomalies.expected: The anodes of these status LEDs need a supply (+3V3 or a switched 3.3 V rail). Their cathodes are driven by the CM4 Ethernet and activity LED lines, so a floating anode means the LEDs cannot light.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet and power/activity indicator LEDs (D4, D14, D23) stay dark because their anode net has no source.
